title: Your camera roll is a personality test
dek: The photos you keep, the ones you delete and the ones you never send. Twelve questions and a verdict on your gallery.

questions.prompt: Your camera roll's most recent screenshot is:

options.label: A price you're pretending not to know

questions.prompt: You're at a party and the host has vanished. The music is still on.

options.label: Start a group photo, someone will edit it
Leave. This was the exit window

questions.prompt: Pick the party you'd actually stay at.

options.label: Glossy, loud, everyone dressed up
options.alt: A warmly lit restaurant interior set for a party

options.label: Neon basement, terrible speakers
options.alt: A dark room lit by neon signs

options.label: A picnic with too much food
options.alt: A picnic blanket with baskets in a park

questions.prompt: If it wasn't posted, did it happen?
I take a photo of the food before anyone eats.
A friend asks you to delete a photo of them from 2019.

options.label: Only if they delete one of you
You'll crop them out and keep it

questions.prompt: Aesthetic is a valid life strategy.
Someone tags you in an old photo. The lighting is a crime.

options.label: Reply with a worse one of them
Save it. That was a good year
Study it for signs of who you are now

questions.prompt: My camera roll is 60% screenshots of things I'll never read.
A house with no books is not a home.
Your storage is full and the phone is choosing violence.

options.label: Delete four hundred photos in one sitting
Start a second account for the overflow

results.name: Y2K
results.blurb: Your camera roll is a night out: flash, motion blur, three good ones and forty you'd never post. You photograph the fun rather than the view. The aesthetic is accidental because you were busy actually being there, which is the most enviable thing about it.
strengths: Finds the fun before the photo
Turns a Tuesday into an occasion
results.watchOut: Not every memory needs a witness. Put the phone down for one hour of it.

results.name: Brat Summer
results.blurb: You've stopped curating. The blurry photo, the undone hair, the terrible angle — posted anyway, because the bit is better than the beauty. You're allergic to trying too hard and you've made not-trying into a whole visual language.
results.watchOut: The joke version of you can become the only version people get. Let one sincere photo through.

results.name: Cottagecore
results.blurb: Your camera roll is a quieter world: light through a window, a mug, a walk, a cat you met. You document the calm because you're actively building it. People think it's an aesthetic. It's actually a coping strategy that happens to look lovely.
strengths: Makes ordinary life feel worth keeping
results.watchOut: The calm can become avoidance. Answer the difficult message before the walk.

results.name: McBling
results.blurb: Your photos are an event. Good lighting, better outfit, a caption you thought about for longer than you'd admit. You like things shiny and you've decided that's not a character flaw. The confidence is real, and it lifts the room.
strengths: Knows what looks good and why
results.watchOut: If the photo is the point, the memory gets thin. Keep one night unrecorded.

results.name: Dark Academia
results.tagline: Moody light, annotations, one good coat
results.blurb: You photograph buildings, books, rain and the corner of a coffee cup with a pen in frame. Your camera roll is a mood board for a life you're still building. You're not pretentious — you're just genuinely more interested in the atmosphere than the event.
results.watchOut: Living it beats styling it. Go to the thing without planning the shot.

results.name: Gym Mirror
results.blurb: Your roll is full of angles, splits, plates and screenshots of programmes. You measure things because measuring works for you. The discipline is genuine, though the mirror selfies suggest you also enjoy being witnessed being disciplined.
strengths: Treats the body as a project, kindly
Quietly competitive in a useful way
results.watchOut: Not everything is a metric. Take a photo you'll like in ten years.

results.name: Food Diary
results.blurb: Your gallery is mostly plates. You photograph what you're about to eat, the table, the menu, the place you'll bring someone next time. Food is how you mark time and how you say you care. The photos are terrible in low light and you post them anyway.
strengths: Finds joy in small daily rituals
Remembers places by what they served
results.watchOut: Eat it while it's hot. The photo can wait and often shouldn't be taken.

results.name: Screenshot Archive
results.tagline: Evidence, receipts and things to read later
results.blurb: Your camera roll is an archive: tweets, articles, messages, a to-do list you photographed in a hurry. You save things because saving feels like doing. Somewhere in there is the exact thing you need, and you'll find it in eighteen months.
results.watchOut: A screenshot is not an action. Pick three and actually do them.

results.name: The Film Roll
results.blurb: You take fewer photos and mean all of them: grain, bad light, one blurry frame of somebody laughing. You wait three weeks for the scans and it's worth it. Nothing gets posted for the algorithm; everything gets kept for the people in it.
strengths: Notices the moment instead of the feed
results.watchOut: Twenty-four shots means you're sometimes not in the photo at all.

results.name: The Pet Folder
results.tagline: Four hundred photos of an animal
results.blurb: Your camera roll has a subfolder that is 90% one creature being extremely ordinary. You show people unsolicited and you do not stop when they look away. Every trip, every bad day, every good light — there is a small animal in the frame somewhere.
strengths: Finds joy in the same small thing daily
results.watchOut: Ask before the fifth photo. Even the dog has boundaries.
